title: Bihar can close its farm performance gap when **4** levers work together: productivity, diversification, market linkages, and delivery execution
subtitle: The operating logic is cumulative rather than sequential: higher output matters only when farmers shift into higher-value crops, connect to stronger buyers, and receive services through reliable state and partner delivery systems.

blocks.title: Farm productivity expands saleable output from the same land base
blocks.body: Evidence focus: yield improvement, irrigation reliability, input quality, agronomy adoption, and lower production risk across Bihar’s core crop systems.

blocks.title: Higher-value diversification improves the crop mix, not just the crop yield
blocks.body: Evidence focus: movement into horticulture and other higher-value crops, stronger gross returns per acre, and lower dependence on a narrow cereal base.

blocks.title: Market linkages raise realization by connecting production to stronger demand channels
blocks.body: Evidence focus: aggregation, grading, storage, buyer access, logistics, and better alignment between what farmers grow and what markets reward.

blocks.title: Delivery execution turns priorities into repeatable farmer-level results
blocks.body: Evidence focus: last-mile extension, program coordination, data-led targeting, partner accountability, and district-level execution that sustains adoption at scale.
